baseline.answer:
**Social recommendation** is the class of recommender-system techniques that explicitly exploit *social information* (friendship links, trust statements, user-generated content, community structures, etc.) in addition to the usual user-item interaction data.  Since the first wave of papers in the mid-2000s, a surprisingly diverse toolbox has been built.  Below is a (non-exhaustive) taxonomy of the major methodological families that have been applied, together with representative publications, key ideas, and typical strengths/limitations.

---

## 1. Matrix-Factorization-Based Approaches with Social Regularization  

| Method | Core Idea | Representative Papers |
|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| **Social MF (SoMF)** | Adds a social-regularization term that forces the latent vectors of socially connected users to be close. | Ma, H., Zhou, D., Liu, C., Lyu, M. R., & King, I. (2008). *Recommender systems with social regularization*. KDD. |
| **TrustMF / TrustSVD** | Extends MF by weighting the social regularizer with explicit trust scores (or inferred trust). | Guo, G., Zhang, J., & Thalmann, D. (2015). *Trust-aware collaborative filtering*. WWW. |
| **Social Bayesian Personalized Ranking (SBPR)** | Bayesian ranking loss + social regularizer for implicit feedback. | Liu, Q., Wu, J., & Zhou, J. (2015). *Social Bayesian personalized ranking*. IJCAI. |
| **Collective Matrix Factorization (CMF)** | Jointly factorizes the user-item rating matrix and the user-user social adjacency matrix. | Singh, A. P., & Gordon, G. J. (2008). *Relational learning via collective matrix factorization*. KDD. |
| **Social Regularized Tensor Factorization** | Extends to context-aware or time-aware tensors while still imposing social smoothness. | Zhang, Y., & Chen, X. (2015). *Social regularized tensor factorization for context-aware recommendation*. TKDE. |

**Why it matters:**  MF-style models are still the workhorse for large-scale industrial systems because they are linear-time in the number of observed interactions and can be trained with stochastic gradient descent (SGD) or alternating least squares (ALS).  The social regularizer is easy to plug in and often yields a modest but consistent lift (≈ 2-5 % in NDCG) when the social graph is dense.

---

## 2. Graph-Based Diffusion / Propagation Models  

| Method | Core Idea | Representative Papers |

| **Social Diffusion (Heat Diffusion, Random Walk with Restart)** | Propagates preference scores over the social network (or a combined user-item-social tripartite graph). | Zhou, T., Ren, J., Medo, M., & Zhang, Y.-C. (2007). *Bipartite network projection and recommendation*. Phys. Rev. E. |
| **Social Influence Propagation (SIP)** | Models influence as a cascade; the final recommendation is the steady-state of the cascade. | Liu, N., & Ma, H. (2010). *Social influence based recommendation*. WSDM. |
